Clusters group municipality x zone x year rows (2016-2023) by profile features only
(IRCA, coverage, rurality, altitude, rainfall, poverty, fiscal and performance indices).
IRCA is utility-supplied ("prestadores") IRCA from INS open data. Outcomes were not used.

```{python}
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
ks = pd.read_csv("outputs/k_selection.csv")
cl = pd.read_parquet("outputs/clusters.parquet")
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-elbow
#| fig-cap: "Elbow plot: k-means inertia for k = 2 to 8. The curve flattens after k = 4."
#| fig-alt: "Line chart of k-means inertia against the number of clusters k from 2 to 8, falling steeply at first and flattening after four clusters."
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 3.5))
ax.plot(ks["k"], ks["inertia"], marker="o")
ax.set_xlabel("number of clusters k"); ax.set_ylabel("inertia")
plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-silhouette
#| fig-cap: "Mean silhouette score by k. Higher means better-separated clusters; all values are modest (below 0.25)."
#| fig-alt: "Line chart of the mean silhouette score against k from 2 to 8; k = 2 is highest and the other values lie close together between 0.17 and 0.20."
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 3.5))
ax.plot(ks["k"], ks["silhouette"], marker="o", color="tab:orange")
ax.set_xlabel("number of clusters k"); ax.set_ylabel("silhouette")
plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-pca
#| fig-cap: "First two principal components of the standardised profile features, coloured by cluster. Descriptive grouping only."
#| fig-alt: "Scatter plot of pc1 against pc2 for all rows, coloured by cluster number, showing four overlapping but distinguishable groups."
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.5, 4.5))
for c, g in cl.groupby("cluster"):
    ax.scatter(g["pc1"], g["pc2"], s=4, alpha=0.5, label=f"cluster {c}")
ax.set_xlabel("pc1"); ax.set_ylabel("pc2"); ax.legend(markerscale=3)
plt.show()
```

## What sets each cluster apart?

Cells are each cluster's mean z-score (standardised within year) per profile feature.
Blue is below the yearly average and red above. Descriptive only.

```{python}
#| label: fig-heatmap
#| fig-cap: "Cluster mean z-scores (within year) of the nine profile features; blue below average, red above."
#| fig-alt: "Heatmap with the nine profile features as rows and the four named clusters as columns; colours run from blue (below the yearly average) to red (above)."
import numpy as np
prof = pd.read_csv("outputs/cluster_profiles.csv").set_index("cluster")
zc = [c for c in prof.columns if c.startswith("z_")]
M = prof[zc].T
M.index = [c[2:] for c in zc]
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 4.8))
v = np.abs(M.values).max()
im = ax.imshow(M.values, cmap="RdBu_r", vmin=-v, vmax=v, aspect="auto")
ax.set_xticks(range(len(M.columns)))
ax.set_xticklabels([prof.loc[c, "name"].replace(", ", ",\n") for c in M.columns], fontsize=8)
ax.set_yticks(range(len(M.index))); ax.set_yticklabels(M.index)
for i in range(M.shape[0]):
    for j in range(M.shape[1]):
        ax.text(j, i, f"{M.values[i, j]:.1f}", ha="center", va="center", fontsize=8)
fig.colorbar(im, label="mean z-score")
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
```

## Outcomes by cluster (descriptive, not used for clustering)

Median per cluster and year; gaps are years the source does not cover (not joined).
Infant mortality changes method in 2017 and Saber 11 has no 2018 or 2021 data.

```{python}
#| label: fig-outcomes
#| fig-cap: "Median infant mortality, Saber 11 mean score and school dropout by cluster and year. Lines break in years without data. Association only; no causal claim."
#| fig-alt: "Three line charts, one per outcome, with a line per cluster over 2016 to 2023; lines have gaps in years with missing data."
oy = pd.read_csv("outputs/outcomes_by_year.csv")
outs = list(oy["outcome"].unique())
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, len(outs), figsize=(4.2 * len(outs), 3.6))
axes = np.atleast_1d(axes)
years = np.arange(oy["year"].min(), oy["year"].max() + 1)
for ax, o in zip(axes, outs):
    for c, g in oy[oy["outcome"] == o].groupby("cluster"):
        s = g.set_index("year")["median"].reindex(years)   # NaN = gap, line breaks
        ax.plot(years, s.values, marker="o", ms=3, color=prof.loc[c, "color"],
                label=prof.loc[c, "name"])
    ax.set_title(o); ax.set_xlabel("year")
axes[0].legend(fontsize=6)
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
```

## Worse water, more infant deaths? A within-cluster check

Median infant mortality (deaths per 1,000 live births) by IRCA band (utility-supplied,
INS open data) within each cluster, with Spearman rho between IRCA and infant mortality
and the number of rows `n` behind it. Only rows with an infant-mortality value count.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-irca-infant
#| tbl-cap: "Spearman rho (IRCA vs infant mortality) and n by cluster, and median infant mortality by IRCA band."
rho = pd.read_csv("outputs/irca_infant.csv")
bins = pd.read_csv("outputs/irca_infant_bins.csv")
names = prof["name"]
rho_t = rho[["cluster", "spearman_rho", "n", "municipalities"]].copy()
rho_t["cluster"] = rho_t["cluster"].map(names)
rho_t["spearman_rho"] = rho_t["spearman_rho"].round(2)
display(rho_t.set_index("cluster"))
med_t = bins.pivot(index="irca_band", columns="cluster", values="median").round(1)
n_t = bins.pivot(index="irca_band", columns="cluster", values="n")
order = [b for b in ["No risk", "Low", "Medium", "High", "Unfit"] if b in med_t.index]
med_t = med_t.loc[order]; n_t = n_t.loc[order]
med_t.columns = [names[c] for c in med_t.columns]
n_t.columns = med_t.columns
print("Median infant mortality by IRCA band:")
display(med_t)
print("Rows (n) behind each cell:")
display(n_t)
```

**This is descriptive and does not establish a causal effect of water safety on infant
mortality.** Within clusters the correlations are weak, and confounders (poverty, health
services, altitude, rurality, the 2017 change in how infant mortality is measured) are not
controlled for.
